title: Position and Movement: Grids, Maps and Directions
seo_title: Grade 5 Position and Movement Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Locate positions on a grid with alphabetical and numerical grid references; locate and give directions to specified positions on a map or grid; describe the movement between positions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 position and movement worksheets: grid references, compass directions and following directions on maps. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Give the direction and the number of squares.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A grid reference names a square by its column letter and row number: C4.
  • Read the letter along the bottom first, then the number up the side.
  • Compass directions: north (N), east (E), south (S), west (W). North-east is between north and east.
  • Directions on a map: say the direction and the number of squares.

Examples

Example

From B2, go 3 squares east and 2 squares north

B → C, D, E

2 → 3, 4

Answer: E4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Row firstLetter first, then number.
East and westEast is on the right of a map with north at the top.
Counting the startCount the moves, not the starting square.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about position and movement?
faq.a: Locate positions on a grid with alphabetical and numerical grid references, and describe the movement between positions on a map or grid.
To find places on a map quickly.

items.q: What is in square C1?
items.e: Go across to column C first, then down to row 1. Square C1 is the library. Reading the number as the column (column A, row 3) gives the fire station.

items.q: What is in square E2?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 2. Square E2 is the chemist. Reading the number as the column (column B, row 5) gives the train station.

items.q: What is in square A3?
items.e: Go across to column A first, then down to row 3. Square A3 is the fire station. Reading the number as the column (column C, row 1) gives the library.

items.q: What is in square F3?
items.e: Go across to column F first, then down to row 3. Square F3 is the bus stop.

items.q: What is in square B4?
items.e: Go across to column B first, then down to row 4. Square B4 is the police station.

items.q: What is in square E5?
items.e: Go across to column E first, then down to row 5. Square E5 is the vet.

items.q: What is in square D4?
items.e: Go across to column D first, then down to row 4. Square D4 is the supermarket.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bakery?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bakery is in column F, row 1: F1. Always write the letter first, so not 1F.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the pool?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The pool is in column A, row 2: A2. Always write the letter first, so not 2A.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the café?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The café is in column E, row 3: E3. Always write the letter first, so not 3E.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the cinema?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The cinema is in column C, row 5: C5. Always write the letter first, so not 5C.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the post office?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The post office is in column E, row 1: E1. Always write the letter first, so not 1E.

items.q: What is the grid reference of the bank?
items.e: Go across to find the letter, then down to find the number. The bank is in column F, row 2: F2. Always write the letter first, so not 2F.

items.q: The park covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The park covers 4 squares: B2, C2, B3 and C3. Letter first, then number, for each square.

items.q: The hospital covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The hospital covers 2 squares: F4 and F5. Letter first, then number, for each square.

items.q: The school covers more than one square. Which squares?
items.e: The school covers 2 squares: A1 and B1. Letter first, then number, for each square.

items.q: Which place covers squares A5 and B5?
items.e: Row 5 is the bottom row. Squares A5 and B5 are the first two squares in it: the train station.

items.q: Which square is empty?
items.e: D2 is in column D, row 2. Nothing is drawn there. C2 is part of the park, E2 is the chemist and D4 is part of the supermarket.

items.q: Which place is in the same row as the pool?
items.e: The pool is in A2, so it is in row 2. The chemist is in E2, also row 2. The fire station is in A3: same column, not the same row.

items.q: Priya says the police station is in 4B. What should she write?
items.e: Priya has the number first. A grid reference gives the letter first (across), then the number (down): B4.

items.q: The oval is ___ of the garden.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The oval is east of the garden. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The tuck shop is ___ of the toilets.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The tuck shop is north of the toilets.

items.q: The art room is ___ of the tuck shop.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The art room is south of the tuck shop.

items.q: The library is ___ of the hall.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The library is east of the hall. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The hall is ___ of the office.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The hall is west of the office. Do not mix up east and west: “Never Eat Soggy Weet-Bix” goes round clockwise: north, east, south, west.

items.q: The bike racks are ___ of the classrooms.
items.e: Use the compass: north is up, south is down, east is right and west is left. The bike racks are south of the classrooms.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the garden?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the library. Going south would give the sandpit.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight west from the garden?
items.e: West is to the left on the map. Go west from the garden, square by square. The first place you reach is the toilets. Going east would give the oval.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north from the sandpit?
items.e: North is up on the map. Go north from the sandpit, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight south from the library?
items.e: South is down on the map. Go south from the library, square by square. The first place you reach is the garden.

items.q: The zebras are ___ of the wild dogs.
items.e: The wild dogs are in C3 and the zebras are in D2. From the wild dogs, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the zebras are north-east of the wild dogs. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-west would be the other way.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the ostriches.
items.e: The ostriches are in C1 and the reptiles are in A3. From the ostriches, go 2 squares left (west) and 2 squares down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the reptiles are south-west of the ostriches. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-east would be the other way.

items.q: The toilets are ___ of the entrance.
items.e: The entrance is in C5 and the toilets are in B4. From the entrance, go 1 square left (west) and 1 square up (north). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the toilets are north-west of the entrance. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: north-east would be the other way.

items.q: The play area is ___ of the seals.
items.e: The seals are in E3 and the play area is in F4. From the seals, go 1 square right (east) and 1 square down (south). The same number each way is a diagonal, so the play area is south-east of the seals. Check east (right) and west (left) carefully: south-west would be the other way.

items.q: The tortoise is ___ of the zebras.
items.e: The zebras are in D2 and the tortoise is in D4. From the zebras, go 2 squares down (south). So the tortoise is south of the zebras.

items.q: The café is ___ of the aviary.
items.e: The aviary is in E1 and the café is in F1. From the aviary, go 1 square right (east). So the café is east of the aviary.

items.q: The lions are ___ of the reptiles.
items.e: The reptiles are in A3 and the lions are in A1. From the reptiles, go 2 squares up (north). So the lions are north of the reptiles.

items.q: The reptiles are ___ of the wild dogs.
items.e: The wild dogs are in C3 and the reptiles are in A3. From the wild dogs, go 2 squares left (west). So the reptiles are west of the wild dogs.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-west from the wild dogs?
items.e: North-west is up and to the left on the map. From the wild dogs (C3), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the meerkats in B2. Going north-east by mistake gives the zebras.

items.q: What is the first place you reach going straight north-east from the entrance?
items.e: North-east is up and to the right on the map. From the entrance (C5), move one square at a time diagonally: the first place is the tortoise in D4. Going north-west by mistake gives the toilets.

items.q: Aisha starts at the red dot in B4. She goes 3 squares east. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at B4. Go 3 squares east to E4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: Ofentse starts at the red dot in E5. She goes 3 squares north. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: Lungile starts at the red dot in F2. He goes 4 squares west. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at F2. Go 4 squares west to B2. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C2.

items.q: Sibusiso starts at the red dot in A1. He goes 3 squares south-east. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 3 squares south-east to D4. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at C3.

items.q: Bongani starts at the red dot in E5. He goes 2 squares north-west, then 1 square north. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 2 squares north-west to C3, then 1 square north to C2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives D2.

items.q: Pieter starts at the red dot in B5. He goes 2 squares north-east, then 2 squares east. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at B5. Go 2 squares north-east to D3, then 2 squares east to F3. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at D4.

items.q: Lethabo starts at the red dot in F1. He goes 2 squares south-west, then 2 squares south. Which square does he finish in?
items.e: Start at F1. Go 2 squares south-west to D3, then 2 squares south to D5. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at E3.

items.q: Tumi starts at the red dot in A3. She goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Which square does she finish in?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 2 squares north to D1. Mixing up north and south gives D5.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 1 square south-east, then 3 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 1 square south-east to B2, then 3 squares east to E2. The gum tree is in E2. Swapping the two numbers of squares gives the sandpit.

items.q: Start at the car park. Go 4 squares north, then 2 squares west. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 4 squares north to F1, then 2 squares west to D1. The swings are in D1. Counting the starting square stops you 1 square short, at the gum tree.

items.q: Priya starts at the red dot. She goes 2 squares east. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at C4. Go 2 squares east to E4. That is square B. If you mix up east and west you land on A.

items.q: Precious starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares north. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E5. Go 3 squares north to E2. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Lwazi starts at the red dot. She goes 3 squares west. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at E2. Go 3 squares west to B2. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Musa starts at the red dot. He goes 3 squares south. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at C1. Go 3 squares south to C4. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Kabelo starts at the red dot. He goes 3 squares east, then 2 squares north. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 3 squares east to D5, then 2 squares north to D3. That is square A. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on B.

items.q: Kgomotso starts at the red dot. She goes 1 square north, then 3 squares west. Where does she finish?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 1 square north to F4, then 3 squares west to C4. That is square D. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Ravi starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares south, then 3 squares east. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at B1. Go 2 squares south to B3, then 3 squares east to E3. That is square C. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Ethan starts at the red dot. He goes 2 squares west, then 3 squares north. Where does he finish?
items.e: Start at E4. Go 2 squares west to C4, then 3 squares north to C1. That is square B. If you count the starting square you stop 1 short, on A.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares north, then 2 squares east. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 2 squares north to A3, then 2 squares east to C3. The gum tree is in C3.

items.q: Start at the BBQ. Go 3 squares east, then 1 square north. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 3 squares east to D3, then 1 square north to D2. The bench is in D2.

items.q: Which directions take you from the gate to the sandpit?
items.e: The gate is in A1 and the sandpit is in E4. A to E is 4 squares east. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the slide to the toilets?
items.e: The slide is in C1 and the toilets are in A4. C to A is 2 squares west. Row 1 to row 4 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the car park to the BBQ?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the BBQ is in B2. F to B is 4 squares west. Row 5 to row 2 is 3 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the rotunda to the kiosk?
items.e: The rotunda is in C5 and the kiosk is in F1. C to F is 3 squares east. Row 5 to row 1 is 4 squares north. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which directions take you from the tap to the skate park?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the skate park is in A5. F to A is 5 squares west. Row 2 to row 5 is 3 squares south. Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the tap to the rotunda?
items.e: The tap is in F2 and the rotunda is in C5. That is 3 squares west and 3 squares south: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares south-west.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the toilets to the swings?
items.e: The toilets are in A4 and the swings are in D1. That is 3 squares east and 3 squares north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 3 squares north-east.

items.q: Which one straight line takes you from the car park to the sandpit?
items.e: The car park is in F5 and the sandpit is in E4. That is 1 square west and 1 square north: the same number each way, so it is a diagonal. Go 1 square north-west.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the BBQ to the swings?
items.e: Start at B2. Go 2 squares east to D2, then 1 square north to D1. That is the swings.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the gate to the rotunda?
items.e: Start at A1. Go 2 squares south to A3, then 1 square east to B3, then 2 squares south to B5, then 1 square east to C5. That is the rotunda.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the rotunda to the sandpit?
items.e: Start at C5. Go 1 square north to C4, then 2 squares east to E4. That is the sandpit.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the car park to the gum tree?
items.e: Start at F5. Go 2 squares north to F3, then 1 square west to E3, then 1 square north to E2. That is the gum tree.

items.q: Which directions describe the dashed path from the skate park to the bench?
items.e: Start at A5. Go 1 square east to B5, then 1 square north to B4, then 2 squares east to D4, then 1 square south to D5. That is the bench.

items.q: How many squares long is the dashed path from the gate to the rotunda?
items.e: Add the squares of each part: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6 squares. Count the moves, not the gate square you start on.

items.q: Tshepo walks from the gate to the rotunda. He moves only north, south, east or west, and only through empty squares. What is the fewest number of squares he can move?
items.e: The gate is in A1 and the rotunda is in C5: 2 squares across and 4 squares up or down. 2 + 4 = 6 squares, and there is a way round through empty squares that is this short. Do not count the starting square.

items.q: Ethan walks from the bench to the BBQ. He moves only north, south, east or west, and only through empty squares. What is the fewest number of squares he can move?
items.e: The bench is in D5 and the BBQ is in B2: 2 squares across and 3 squares up or down. 2 + 3 = 5 squares, and there is a way round through empty squares that is this short. Do not count the starting square.

items.q: Which directions take you from the BBQ to the sandpit without walking through the pond?
items.e: Start at B2. Go 2 squares south to B4, then 3 squares east to E4. That is the sandpit, and the path never enters the pond (C3 and D3). “1 south, 3 east, 1 south” walks through the pond.

items.q: Which directions take you from the swings to the bench without walking through the pond?
items.e: Start at D1. Go 1 square east to E1, then 4 squares south to E5, then 1 square west to D5. That is the bench, and the path never enters the pond (C3 and D3). “4 south” walks through the pond. “1 west, 4 south, 1 east” walks through the pond.

items.q: Lwazi walks from the rotunda: 1 north, 2 east. She reaches the sandpit. Which directions take her back the same way?
items.e: To go back the same way, do the moves in reverse order and turn each direction to its opposite: 2 west, 1 south.

items.q: Mbali walks from the car park: 2 north, 1 west, 1 north. She reaches the gum tree. Which directions take her back the same way?
items.e: To go back the same way, do the moves in reverse order and turn each direction to its opposite: 1 south, 1 east, 2 south.

items.q: What is between the hall and the office?
items.e: Find the hall and the office. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the library.

items.q: What is between the library and the car park?
items.e: Find the library and the car park. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the office.

items.q: What is between the tuck shop and the art room?
items.e: Find the tuck shop and the art room. They are in the same column. The place in the middle of them is the toilets.

items.q: What is between the playground and the gate?
items.e: Find the playground and the gate. They are in the same row. The place in the middle of them is the sandpit.

items.q: What is between the toilets and the playground?
items.e: Find the toilets and the playground. They are in the same column. The place in the middle of them is the art room.

items.q: Which place is next to the bike racks?
items.e: Next to means touching, side by side. The classrooms are just above the bike racks. The gate is 2 squares away.

items.q: The tuck shop is next to two places. What are they?
c: the toilets and the art room
items.e: Look at the squares touching the tuck shop: the hall is just above it and the toilets are just below it. The square on its right is empty.

items.q: Which place is next to the oval?
items.e: The car park touches the top of the oval. The garden and the office do not touch it: there is a gap.

items.q: What is in the top right corner of the map?
items.e: Top means the top row. Right means the right side. The car park is in the top right corner. The hall is in the top left.

items.q: What is in the bottom left corner of the map?
items.e: Bottom means the bottom row. Left means the left side. The playground is in the bottom left corner.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. What is the grid reference of the flying fox?
items.e: Go across to column F, then down to row 2: F2. Letter first, then number.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. What is in square B4?
items.e: Column B, row 4 is the archery. Reading the number as the column (column D, row 2) gives the dining hall.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. Which squares does the lake cover?
items.e: The lake is in columns D and E, rows 3 and 4: D3, E3, D4 and E4.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. From the campfire, the class walks 1 square north-east, then 1 square east. Where are they?
items.e: Start at A3. Go 1 square north-east to B2, then 1 square east to C2. C2 is part of the dining hall.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. Which directions take you from the toilets to the office?
items.e: The toilets are in A5 and the office is in D1. A to D is 3 squares east. Row 5 to row 1 is 4 squares north.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. The archery is ___ of the campfire.
items.e: The campfire is in A3 and the archery is in B4: 1 square right (east) and 1 square down (south). That is south-east.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. Each square on the map is 50 metres. How far is it from the campfire straight south to the toilets?
items.e: From A3 to A5 is 2 squares. 2 × 50 = 100 metres. Counting the campfire square too gives 3 squares, or 150 metres.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. Each square is 50 metres. Pieter walks from the archery 4 squares east, then 2 squares north to the flying fox. How far does he walk?
items.e: He walks 4 + 2 = 6 squares. 6 × 50 = 300 metres. Only counting the east part gives 4 × 50 = 200 metres.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. Ruan is at the toilets, facing north. He makes a quarter turn clockwise, then walks 3 squares. What does he reach?
items.e: Facing north, a quarter turn clockwise makes him face east. 3 squares east of A5 is D5: the canoes.

items.q: Grade 4 is on school camp. What is the first place you reach going straight north-east from the archery?
items.e: North-east is up and to the right. From B4: C3 is empty, then D2 is the dining hall. North-west would give the campfire.
